name: argument-parser-positive-test-e41e5b8a0a/defaultable-v

spec_references.heading: Subset restrictions / Invocations / Named and default arguments
spec_references.quote: Named arguments and omitted defaultable arguments are supported for function calls when the callee has an atomic function type with a known parameter signature.

spec_references.heading: Subset restrictions / Invocations / Other invocation restrictions

reason: The case requires command-line entry-point argument binding: @args supplies the string 1 to required int main parameter val, and the remaining five main parameters must receive defaults. The subset specifies function signatures and default omission for function calls, but does not cover command-line argument parsing or main entry-point parameter binding. Supported defaultable syntax alone does not establish support for this whole argument-parser case.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line argument conversion and binding to a parameterized main function, including omitted defaultable entry-point arguments (not covered by subset10).
test_design_notes: Mixed case: required/defaultable parameter declarations, numeric/string literals, concatenation, and value:toString method calls are supported constructs.
The @args ["1"] marker and expected output make entry-point argument parsing essential; there is no ordinary source-level call to main.
io:println and @output are instrumentation and do not independently justify feature classification.
